target.title: fix(signal): add timeouts to container REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container REST requests already had a timeout around the fetch call, but the timer was cleared as soon as response headers arrived. A slow or hanging response body could still block REST send/status and attachment paths indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing timeout active until callers finish reading or releasing the response body. The change preserves the existing fetch helper, bounded body readers, cleanup path, and caller upload/attachment semantics.

## User Impact

If the signal-cli REST container returns headers and then stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request during body reading instead of leaving Signal operations pending forever.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed: 62 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed.
- Remote Testbox/Crabbox validation was attempted, but the local wrapper rejected the selected crabbox binary during sanity checks, so focused local wrapper tests were used instead.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Session trajectory artifacts (`.trajectory.jsonl` + `.trajectory-path.json`) were handled inconsistently, and destructively, across the session lifecycle:

1. **Delete** (dashboard / `sessions.delete` RPC) archived the transcript but left the trajectory pair orphaned on disk forever (the original [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200) defect).
2. **Reset paths** either deleted the trajectory outright (destroying the forensic tool-call record, flagged as a P1 by the automated review on this PR) or left it at its live name to be misclassified later.
3. The **typed `/new` and `/reset`** commands (and the implicit daily/idle rollover) went through a code path with no trajectory handling at all, so fixes applied to the other reset doors never reached the path users actually type.

## What This Change Does

One consistent model: **trajectory artifacts shadow their transcript**. Whenever a session's transcript is archived with a `.reset.<ts>` or `.deleted.<ts>` suffix, the trajectory runtime file and pointer are renamed with the byte-identical suffix in the same operation (shared `nowMs`), never unlinked:

- A `TrajectoryArtifactDisposal` union threads the disposal mode through the cleanup helpers: `{ mode: "tombstone", reason, nowMs }` for user-visible lifecycle events, with rename-in-place semantics under the same `withTrajectoryPathLock` retire turn.
- All three lifecycle doors are coupled: `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` (delete), `resetSessionEntryLifecycle` (dashboard New Session button), and the typed-command rollover path `initSessionState` → `commitReplySessionInitialization`, plus the internal self-heal path `persistSessionResetLifecycle`.
- The referenced-sessions guard snapshot is taken **inside the locked store mutator** (`referencedSessionIdsAtSwap`), closing a race where an unlocked re-read after two await points could see a concurrent writer's row and silently skip the tombstone.
- **External trajectory directories** (`OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`): the pair is tombstoned in place only under proven ownership (registry-owned, or the session's own pointer file names the target); unproven files in an operator-configured directory are left untouched. The retention sweep follows tombstone directories, so aging works there too.
- **No new retention code.** Tombstoned trajectories reuse the existing `.reset.<ts>` / `.deleted.<ts>` suffix conventions and age out with the existing archived-transcript sweep.

## Why rename instead of delete on reset

No merged commit or confirmed-maintainer comment currently states reset-vs-trajectory policy explicitly, but the record strongly and repeatedly converges on one answer: reset must preserve trajectory records via rename/archive, never delete them outright. This is proposed directly in [#90707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90707) (with a concrete forensics-loss incident as motivation), implemented the same way in the still-open [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) (after two prior closed-unmerged attempts at the identical shape, [#93319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93319) and [#94895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94895)), echoed by the broader "never `rm` a session file, only move/rename" position in [#56609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609), and most directly, flagged as a P1 blocker on this very branch by the automated reviewer, which asked explicitly to "preserve or archive pre-reset trajectories instead of deleting them." This PR's tombstone-rename on the runner-driven `/reset` path is our attempt to satisfy that converging intent without waiting on #94593 to land, since the two changes touch adjacent but distinct code paths (delete-lifecycle cleanup vs. the shared reset-archive helper) and reconciling them is better done as a maintainer-guided follow-up than by blocking this fix on an unrelated open PR.

## Evidence

Test gates on the final head: `session-accessor.test.ts` 73/73, `session.test.ts` 143/143, adjacent lifecycle suites 24/24 (240 total), typecheck (`tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test`) clean, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Every fix commit is red-proven: the concurrent-writer race test and the entry-level typed-`/reset` test (entering through `initSessionState`, not the inner function) each fail against the pre-fix code exactly as observed live and pass after.

Live validation on a v2026.6.10 production deployment (session ids redacted):

```
typed /reset:
  <sid-A>.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory-path.json.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z

dashboard delete: same trio shape with .deleted.<ts>, session key removed, clean re-mint on next message

typed /new with OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR set (trajectory lives outside the sessions dir):
  sessions dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>  +  <sid-B>.trajectory-path.json.reset.<ts>
  external dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>   (renamed in place, same timestamp)
```

## Scope notes

- `applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` (the batched background-maintenance mutation used by the session reaper, cleanup service, and heartbeat runner) is deliberately not touched: its removed-session cleanup already routes through the trajectory-coupled maintenance helpers, and unreferenced pairs are reclaimed by the age-based prune, which is the correct model for background reaping (no user action to timestamp-couple to).
- [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) partially overlaps on intent (reset-time preservation) but implements it in the shared reset-archive helper; this PR covers the delete lifecycle and the typed-command rollover door. If #94593 lands first we are happy to rebase and drop any overlap, and vice versa.

## User Impact

Deleting or resetting a session, from any surface, now leaves a complete archived trio with one shared timestamp instead of orphaned or destroyed trajectory files. Post-incident forensics of tool calls survives resets. Existing retention behavior and bounds are unchanged.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. - **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` does not check `lastRunWasManual`.   4. **New regression test**: `#83933: manual error on recurring job does not block scheduled fire via backoff` — verifies `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` returns `undefined` for manual errors, `isRunnableJob()` returns `true` within theoretical backoff window, `recomputeNextRunsForMaintenance()` computes natural cadence (not backoff floor), and control case confirms scheduled errors still apply backoff ✅

- **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` on recurring job (requires working LLM in Docker). Multi-node cluster, production load, actual delivery to chat channels.




## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: With the guard disabled (`false && opts?.isManual`), the new regression test fails — a manual ok run rewrites `nextRunAtMs` to the natural next fire (`endedAt + 60s`) instead of preserving the pending backoff window (`endedAt + 30min`), while the other regression tests still pass. Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.

```bash

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

```


- **New regression test**: `#83538: manual ok run on recurring job preserves pending scheduled error-backoff window` — sets up an `every` 60s job with a pending backoff window (`nextRunAtMs = endedAt + 30min`, `consecutiveErrors: 2`), runs a manual OK completion (`isManual: true`), and asserts the backoff `nextRunAtMs` is preserved (not reset to the natural next run). The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI end-to-end for this specific success-path branch (a manual `ok` outcome requires a working LLM provider in Docker; earlier Docker CLI proofs cover the manual-run survival/backoff paths). Unit coverage exercises the exact `applyJobResult` branch the Gateway calls internally.

target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams file consent uploads validated the SharePoint consent URL, then performed the upload PUT without a request deadline. If the upload request never completed, the accepted file delivery path could remain pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded consent upload timeout using the existing timer timeout resolver, and keep the abort timer active until the upload request finishes. The SSRF host/IP validation and upload headers/body semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

When a Teams file consent upload stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request instead of waiting forever, so the file delivery flow can fail quickly and surface the error path.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts` passed: 64 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts` passed.
- Remote Testbox/Crabbox validation was attempted, but the local wrapper rejected the selected crabbox binary during sanity checks, so focused local wrapper tests were used instead.
